Joint consideration of draft reports on the revision of the EU ETS Directive
On 1 October 2026, ENVI Members considered two closely related draft reports: on the revision of the EU Emission Trading System (EU ETS Directive) and on the regulation to simplify and streamline monitoring, reporting and verification of the CO2 emissions for the maritime transport (MRV Regulation). These two files are important elements of a legislative package implementing the EU's legally binding 2040 climate target.
In the draft report on the revision of the EU ETS Directive, the rapporteur seeked to maintain a strong decarbonization signal while giving more flexibility by reducing the LRF from 3.7% to 3.4% between 2031 - 2035, and then raising it from 1.7% to 2.3% between 2036 and 2040; on conditionality he suggested a more prudent approach than the one proposed by the Commission, starting with additional conditionality only for the additional free allowances; and he supplemented the proposals to protect frontrunners with several additional elements, such as an increase in the number of free allowances for the top 10% most efficient installations in each sector. He also deleted the proposed by the Commission opt-out for Member States regarding the municipal waste incineration.
In the draft report on MRV Regulation, the rapporteur took over the Commission proposal since the main elements of the rules concerning shipping are addressed in the main EU ETS proposal, where he suggested phasing out the current derogations until 2040 instead of prolonging them to 2035 as in the Commission proposal.
